new_jobs.description:
Description

Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

UNC Health is seeking a dedicated Social Worker
to join our Emergency Department team. This role supports patients and families in a fast‑paced, high‑acuity environment, providing crisis intervention, resource coordination, and comprehensive psychosocial support. The ED team currently works four 10-hour shifts per week, offering a dynamic schedule within a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting.

Summary

A Social Worker - MSW (Inpatient) is a crucial member of the healthcare team, providing comprehensive support and services to patients and their families. They are responsible for conducting assessments, supporting patient-centered care plans, facilitating resources, monitoring progress, advocating for patients, actively listening to their concerns, respecting individuality, building trust, performing risk segmentation, carrying out delegated work, coordinating care, and communicating with payers.

Responsibilities

Assessments: Conduct thorough assessments of patients' mental, emotional, and social well-being to evaluate their needs and identify any barriers to their overall functioning. This includes assessing their support systems, coping mechanisms, mental health conditions, and psychosocial factors.
Patient-Centered Care Plans: Collaborate with providers, patients, their families, and the healthcare team on individualized care plans that align with patients' goals, preferences, and values. Resource Facilitation: Connect patients and their families with community resources, mental health services, support groups, and other relevant programs. This includes assisting with referrals for psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and coordinating care with other providers.
Progress Monitoring & Evaluation: Continuously monitor and evaluate the progress of patients' care plans to assess their response to interventions, measure outcomes, and make necessary adjustments. Collaborate with the healthcare team to ensure appropriate care progression, follow-up and continuity of care.
Advocacy: Advocate for patients' needs within the healthcare system and the community. This involves ensuring access to appropriate treatment, facilitating communication between patients and their healthcare team, and addressing any barriers or concerns that may impact the patient's well-being.
Active Listening: Engage in active listening to understand patients' experiences, concerns, and emotions. Provide a safe and non-judgmental space for patients to express themselves and offer empathy, validation, and support.
Respect for Individuality: Recognize and respect the unique values, beliefs, and cultural backgrounds of each patient. Tailor interventions and support to align with their individual needs and preferences, taking into account their cultural, social, and spiritual backgrounds.
Building Trust: Build trust-based relationships with patients and their families by demonstrating empathy, confidentiality, and professionalism. Foster open communication, collaboration, and a therapeutic alliance.
Risk Segmentation: Utilize risk segmentation strategies to identify patients who may require additional support or interventions based on their medical, psychological, and social risk factors. This helps prioritize resources and interventions for those who need them most.
Tasks or Interventions: Carry out specific tasks or interventions as delegated by the healthcare team.
Delegated Work: Collaborate with other members of the healthcare team to carry out delegated work, such as coordinating referrals, conducting follow-up assessments, and providing ongoing support to patients and their families.
Care Coordination: Coordinate care across different providers and settings to ensure seamless transitions and continuity of care. This may involve facilitating communication, sharing information, and advocating for the patient's needs.
Payer Communication: Communicate with payers, such as insurance companies or government agencies, to provide necessary information for authorization of services, reimbursement, or other documentation requirements.

Other Information

Other information:

Education Requirements

Master's Degree in Social Work

Licensure/Certification Requirements

None required

Professional Experience Requirements

Two (2) years health care experience strongly preferred

Knowledge/Skills/and Abilities Requirements

Knowledge of mental health conditions, diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based treatment modalities
Strong assessment and diagnostic skills
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Ability to collaborate effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team
Empathy, compassion, and cultural sensitivity
Strong organizational and time management skills
Ability to maintain confidentiality and adhere to ethical guidelines

About Butterworth Hospital

Right in the heart of Grand Rapids, you’ll find a nationally recognized hospital for patient quality and safety and the regional leader in full-service hospitals. Scope of work

Utilizes clinical judgment and expertise to coordinate care management/behavioral health interventions. Develops strategies to ensure cost effective, quality care outcomes to patients with complex care needs. Identifies options for levels of care for individuals and populations of patients, focusing on strategies that will promote optimal health. Assesses, plans, monitors, and provides therapeutic interventions as appropriate. Collaborates with patient and family to facilitate understanding of diagnosis and to provide therapeutic interventions to support necessary lifestyle and behavior changes. Partner with patients, families, and other health care providers to ensure understanding the impact the disease or illness has on the patient's mental and emotional health. Respond to crisis situations and engage with patients and families to access the appropriate level of care across the continuum. Emphasis of duties may vary depending upon area of assignment.

WE TRANSFORM LIVES.

Everything we do is designed to improve the quality of life of the people in the state of Illinois, across the nation, and around the world. Through learning partnerships that extend knowledge and change lives, University of Illinois Extension provides educational programs aimed at making life better, healthier, safer, and more profitable for individuals and their communities. Skills in communicating and collaborating with all audiences.

Work closely with the PRIDE Program Administrator to support program goals, ensure high-quality service delivery, and maintain the effectiveness and integrity of the PRIDE program. Oversee assigned projects, manage continuous quality improvement activities, and support core program operations. Supervise trainers and support staff, act as a liaison between PRIDE, DCFS, and private child welfare agencies, and, in collaboration with the Senior Statewide Director of Workforce Development, provide program leadership coverage in the Program Administrator's absence. Project Management & Program Support

Manage assigned projects to ensure timely completion, providing regular updates to the program administrator. In collaboration with Training Coordinators, oversee program schedules and trainer assignments. Support the PRIDE program’s use of technology and the Learning and Development Center (LDC) for data collection and reporting.

Administrative and Supervisory Responsibilities

Supervise a team of trainers and support staff, ensure effective workflow and provide coaching, observation, and feedback to trainers. Serve as a liaison with DCFS, private child welfare agencies, and other stakeholders, attending and presenting at meetings as needed. Approve trainer billing, tracking and/or approving staff time off and reviewing and approving travel justifications. Ensure the program’s accurate completion of registration and attendance reports, manage the PRIDE shared email mailbox, and promptly follow up on inquiries. In the absence of the Program Administrator, act as the program lead, including providing short-term supervision as needed to Training Coordinators. May co-facilitate training sessions when programmatic staffing needs require it. Facilitate regularly scheduled trainer staff development opportunities and events, reviews training performance, data trends and outcomes, curriculum and trainer facilitation strengths, and areas needing improvement.

Collaboration and Curriculum Updates

Collaborate with other Workforce Development Programs, the Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS), and DCFS vendors to coordinate curriculum updates and other projects. This includes working with trainers and curriculum designers on needed curriculum updates and supporting effective caregiver training. Ensure a varied representation of trainers in curriculum update workgroups.

Provide participants, trainers, and licensing workers with general support for navigating PRIDE program trainings within the Learning Management System (LMS) used by DCFS. Collaborate with other Workforce Development program leadership to store, periodically review and update PRIDE caregiver curricula in alignment with Workforce Development processes and procedures. Monitor the LMS registration/attendance report to ensure trainer compliance with attendance tracking and managing data points for reporting training outcomes. Utilize university systems to monitor and approve trainer billing and manage staff time off hours as assigned.

Perform other duties as assigned, which are within the scope of the responsibilities enumerated above. This may include supporting the PRIDE program leadership team during absence of other PRIDE leadership positions.

Statewide travel is required.

Work Schedule, Travel, or Other Job Expectations
Statewide travel is required Minimum Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree. Proficiency in technology, familiarity with Learning Management Systems, knowledge of Power BI, Excel, and other data management software, tracking, and reporting tools. Three (3) or more years of experience overseeing, managing, or supervising direct foster care operations. Three (3) or more years of experience as an Illinois PRIDE trainer.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of foster care practices in Illinois. Strong organizational and problem-solving skills, with an ability to exercise independent judgment and make effective decisions. Excellent customer service interpersonal skills, effective communication, and the ability to follow instructions.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams) and Zoom, skilled in managing PDFs with Adobe Acrobat Reader. Skilled in data entry and managing workflows to meet deadlines efficiently.
Leadership and team management skills with skills in strategic planning, generating analytical reports, and engaging stakeholders, and adaptable in high-pressure environments with competing priorities.

Position Summary

The Programs Manager provides day-to-day leadership and oversight of The Arc’s programs and the staff who deliver them. This hands-on management position is responsible for staff supervision, scheduling, program coordination, quality, logistics, and troubleshooting.
The Programs Manager ensures programs are appropriately staffed, organized, engaging, safe, and responsive to participant needs. The position requires someone who can manage multiple priorities, support and develop staff, and step directly into classes and participant support when coverage is needed.
The Programs Manager works closely with the Assistant Director on participant services and the Program Quality and Compliance Coordinator on documentation, quality assurance, and compliance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Staff and Program Management

Supervise, coach, schedule, and support assigned program staff.
Establish clear expectations and address staff performance concerns in collaboration with the Executive Director.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, training, and development of program staff.
Coordinate daily program operations, staffing, schedules, locations, transportation, supplies, and other logistics.
Serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day program and staffing issues and arrange coverage for absences.
Promote a collaborative, accountable, respectful, and participant-centered work environment.

Program Quality and Participant Support

Oversee class and activity content and work with staff to provide meaningful, engaging, and accessible programming.
Ensure programs promote participant choice, independence, community inclusion, skill development, and individual goals.
Observe programs and provide staff with ongoing coaching and support.
Respond to participant, family, and stakeholder questions or concerns related to program operations.
Provide direct participant support and step into classes, activities, transportation, or other program roles when coverage is needed.
Identify opportunities to strengthen existing programs and develop new activities.

Documentation, Safety, and Compliance

Ensure staff complete required attendance, progress notes, service records, and other documentation accurately and on time.
Work with the Program Quality and Compliance Coordinator to address documentation, training, quality assurance, and compliance concerns.
Ensure staff follow participant plans, organizational policies, safety procedures, and program requirements.
Respond appropriately to incidents, emergencies, and operational concerns and communicate significant issues to the Executive Director.
Participate in quality assurance and continuous improvement activities.

Collaboration and Organizational Support

Coordinate with the Assistant Director regarding participant needs, ISPs, service authorizations, and case management entities.
Participate in staff and leadership meetings, organizational planning, and program development.
Build positive relationships with participants, families, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Perform other related duties as assigned in support of The Arc’s mission and programs.

Qualifications

Experience supervising staff and coordinating programs, preferably in developmental disability services, human services, education, recreation, or a related setting.
Strong leadership, communication, organizational, scheduling, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple programs, employees, locations, and priorities while remaining flexible, person-centered, and solution focused.
Experience supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and knowledge of person-centered practices.
Ability to learn and use scheduling, documentation, and communication systems.
Ability to complete and maintain required training and credentials for direct services.
Valid driver's license and ability to meet organizational driving as needed .

Working Conditions and Expectations

This is an on-site position with a regular Monday – Friday, 9 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. schedule
. The Programs Manager must be able and willing to move between program locations, participate actively in classes and community activities, provide direct coverage when needed, and respond to changing operational needs. Occasional evening and weekend work is required.

The Programs Manager is expected to demonstrate professionalism, reliability, sound judgment, flexibility, respect for participant choice and self-determination, and commitment to the mission and values of The Arc.

Company Description

At NATIVE HEALTH, we strive to provide the best health care available for urban American Indians, Alaska Natives, and other individuals who generally experience barriers to health and wellness services.

Mission:
To provide accessible holistic patient centered care, to empower our community to achieve the highest quality health and well-being.

Vision:
Healthy People in Healthy Communities.

NATIVE HEALTH Benefits and Perks Include:

Medical, Vision, and Dental Insurance
Retirement Benefits - Up to 5% Matching Contribution
Paid Time Off/Sick Leave
Paid Holidays (12)
Tuition Reimbursement and Educational Leave
Employee Recognition Program
Starting Annual Pay: $54,142.40

Job Description

The Outreach and Enrollment (OE) Program Coordinator directs and manages NATIVE HEALTH’s Connecting Kids to Coverage (CKC) Outreach and Enrollment program and the SNAP CMS program. The position oversees a team of Outreach & Enrollment Specialists (OES) across all NATIVE HEALTH locations; ensures program, grant, budget, and reporting requirements are met; and serves as the primary liaison to the funder, community partners, and stakeholders. The coordinator is also a visible community advocate for access to enrollment assistance and education. The Outreach and Enrollment Program Coordinator reports to the Health Services Director.

Evaluation:
Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with provisions of the NATIVE HEALTH Employee Handbook on evaluations.

Essential Functions:
Essential functions as defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act may include the following tasks, knowledge, skills, and other characteristics. This list of tasks is not a comprehensive listing of all functions and tasks performed by position in this class and are subject to change.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

Program Leadership and Operation: Provides direction and oversight of the planning and operation of the Connecting Kids to Coverage (CKC) Outreach and Enrollment in alignment with NATIVE HEALTH’s mission, values and strategic plan.

Measure of Success:

Ensures cooperative agreement goals, objectives, activities, and evaluation requirements are met.
Coordinates outreach and enrollment services with other NATIVE HEALTH programs and external partners, including schools, school districts, and public and private organizations
Ensures clients and patients have optimal access to enrollment assistance and education.
Coordinates a community advisory board that represents the populations served by the funded program and provides ongoing guidance.
Maintains collaborative relationships with councils and boards, including the National Council of Urban Indian Health (NCUIH), National Indian Health Board (NIHB), and Arizona Alliance for Community Health Centers (AACHC).
Staff Leadership and Development: Leads, coaches, mentors, and supervises staff to support engagement and achievement of organizational and cooperative agreement goals.

Measures of Success:

Ensure staff understand and demonstrate NATIVE HEALTH’s mission and values.
Provides appropriate orientation, training, and ongoing development.
Ensures clients and patients have optimal access to enrollment assistance and education.
Ensures staff maintain current knowledge of Medicaid (Arizona AHCCCS), the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and the Health Insurance Marketplace through required training, seminars, and workshops.
Monitors productivity benchmarks, program deliverables, and core competencies.
Provides timely, constructive performance feedback.
Ensure staff attain and maintain required Certified Application Counselor and Community Health Worker (CHW) certifications.
Completes all performance evaluations for all direct reports.
Engage staff in delivering a patient experience that surpasses expectations.
Program Compliance, Budget, and Performance: Manages program compliance, budget performance reporting, and outcome evaluation.

Measures of Success:

Monitors program spending and make programmatic adjustments to ensure budget conformity.
Uses, data, reports, and trends to evaluate, manage, and improve services.
Completes and submits all required quarterly, annual, financial, and evaluation reports on time.
Monitors goals and objectives and implements and evaluates strategies to increase program activity and effectiveness.
Outreach, Enrollment, and Community Partnerships: Ensures accountable delivery of outreach enrollment assistance, and education to clients and communities.

Measures of Success:

Identifies community events to provide community outreach in support of program goals and objectives.
Oversees coordination of event logistics including staff assignment, event set up and tear down, providing outreach and marketing materials and all necessary elements for a successful event.
Serves as the primary liaison to existing and prospective partner agencies and coordinates outreach and enrollment activities.
Coordinates and collaborates with Outreach and Enrollment team members, patients, and families to meet program requirements.
Implement national enrollment initiatives.
Produces multimedia marketing and educational materials for clients.
Supports the organization as needed.

KNOWLEGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Ability to supervise, mentor and coach personnel and provide a positive team-oriented environment.
Expert knowledge of eligibility requirements for Arizona Medicaid, Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and Health Insurance Marketplace.
Knowledge of the cultural, social, and economic background of the American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) and minority populations.
Experience in grants and project management.
Ability to analyze and evaluate data and reports.
Strong customer service skills and the ability to handle difficult situations.
Flexibility to work late hours or weekends when necessary.
Ability to work effectively with government departments, community organizations, agencies, and the general community.
Proficiency with computer-based applications such as MS 365, Adobe, and the health-e-Arizona Plus system.
Effective oral and written communication skills.
Cultural competence and the ability to work with a diverse workforce and client population.
Openness to change and willingness to lead change within the organization.
Professional integrity and an excellent work ethic.
Ability to organize, plan, work independently, take initiative, manage competing priorities, and address concerns and issues effectively.
Ability to network, develop meaningful collaborations, and coordinate activities across multiple programs and organizations.
Knowledge of community resources.
Ability to protect confidential information and maintain the trust of patients, families, and the agency.

Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree in business, health administration, public health, or a related field is required. A master’s degree is preferred.
Minimum of two years of experience relative to Medicaid and CHIP, outreach, education and enrollment services.
Minimum of two years of supervisory and mentoring staff experience is preferred.
Two years of experience with fiscal oversight of government programs, contracts and/or grant preferred.
Must maintain Certified Application Counselor with CMS and remain current on Medicaid, CHIP, and marketplace training.
Must obtain a Community Health Worker (CHW) certification.
Must maintain active enrollment as a Health-e-Arizona Plus Assistor.
Must have a broad understanding of Medicaid, CHIP, and outreach and enrollment best practices, strategies, and community resources.

Standard Employment Requirements:

Must possess a valid and unrestricted Arizona driver’s license (within 30 days of hire if applicant is from out-of-state) with no DUI/DWI or reckless driving convictions in the last five years. No more than two at-fault accidents in the last three years. Must maintain a valid Arizona driver’s license during employment. Must be insurable under NATIVE HEALTH’s liability auto policy.
Must pass a criminal background check and obtain a Class I Fingerprint Clearance Card within the initial ninety (90) calendar days of employment and retain a valid card while employed with NATIVE HEALTH.
Must pass substance abuse testing upon employment and submit to random testing during employment.
Must provide an updated immunization (IZ) record at the time of employment.
Must have a current (within 12 months) Tuberculosis (TB) skin report upon employment and provide an annual update.
Must obtain Basic Life Support (BLS) certification within (90) calendar days of employment and maintain certification during employment.

Native Health complies with all state and federal requirements, including EEOC requirements.09/2026

About Houston-Galveston Area Council  

The Houston-Galveston Area Council is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country with a diverse service area of 13 counties and more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region, addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every single day.  

We make decisions that affect our transportation system, ensure the safety and well-being of our seniors, connect people to jobs, help families recover from natural disasters, preserve water quality for our children, and so much more. We work to make the region a great place to live, work, and thrive. 

What will I be doing?

The Houston-Galveston Area Council (H-GAC) is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Senior Program Coordinator to join and support the Air Quality Team within the Metropolitan Planning & Analysis Division. This position will primarily under the direction of the Air Quality Program Manager and the Director of the Houston-Galveston Clean Cities Coalition to help to support, and at times lead, regional air quality efforts to partner with stakeholders and advance regional clean transportation initiatives, primarily through work with two H-GAC programs – the Houston-Galveston Clean Cities Coalition and the Clean Vehicles Program.

Key Responsibilities

Supporting activities related to the Houston-Galveston Clean Cities Coalition to help stakeholders understand, plan for, and deploy clean vehicle technologies that advance regional, state, and national air quality goals; enhance the nation’s energy security; and support economic prosperity.
Helping to support, and at times leading, efforts related to H-GAC’s vehicle replacement programs, including the Clean Vehicles Program, through the management of program applications, sub agreements, project documentation, site visits, and data reports, and other tasks.
Working collaboratively with local governments, transportation agencies, state and federal partners, community organizations, businesses, universities, and other regional stakeholders to advance practical strategies that improve air quality and support a healthier, more sustainable region
Building professional relationships across public, private, and nonprofit sectors.
Supporting the efforts of local, state, and federal agencies and stakeholders to improve air quality and transportation in the H-GAC service area.
Researching funding opportunities, preparing and submitting grant applications, and developing then implementing the resulting projects or programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, alternative fuels, zero-emission vehicle technologies, and related infrastructure.
Familiarity with the heavy-duty trucking and/or school bus transportation sectors
Project management experience bridging public and private sectors.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
Creative problem-solving skills and innovative outreach strategies
Proficient multitasker able to manage long-term projects with minimal supervision.
Experience in grant research and successfully applying for grant funding.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, and collaboration tools such as Asana.
Bilingual (English/Vietnamese or English/Spanish) a plus.

Bachelor’s degree in environmental, business, project management, or related field.
Five (5) years of experience working with government at all levels, nonprofits, or in positions similar duties.

The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. NYC Service is a division of the Mayor’s Office that provides meaningful access, opportunity, and resources for communities to come together and answer the call to serve NYC. Oversee approximately 30 AmeriCorps members serving at host sites across the City, supporting members throughout their service term.
Conduct in-person site visits and ensure member compliance with AmeriCorps procedures and processes.
Manage relationships with host site supervisors and NYC Service AmeriCorps members.

A Pathway to Housing for Homeless Veterans- Insight Housing Roads Home program assists low-income Veteran families experiencing homelessness to attain housing placement and housing stability. The League of Women Voters of Washington (LWVWA) is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to empowering voters and defending democracy. new_jobs.description:
Social Work / Custody and Removal Coordinator

Minimum Qualifications Summary

Certification & Education

Degree issuing institution and or program must be accredited by an entity recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.

Bachelor’s degree in Social work, Psychology, or an equivalent degree.
Master’s degree or an equivalent advanced degree preferred but not required
Fluent in English and Spanish, written and oral

Experience Required

At least two (2) years of related experience (e.g., experience providing services to victims, trauma-informed programming, experience working with immigrants or foreignborn individuals) and have knowledge of program objectives, policies, procedures and requirements conducting a case management program at a local level.
Experience working in or with victims or individuals in a confinement or custodial setting.
At least two (2) years of experience providing services to vulnerable populations.
Experience with and an understanding of situations that contribute to family/individual stress, problems and crisis situations
Fluent in English and Spanish, written and oral

Job Objective

The Custody and Resource Coordinator (CRC) assists ERO Field Office and detention facility staff in maintaining a safe detention environment. The CRC also provides services and support to individuals on issues that commonly affect the ICE detained population and ICE mission such as responsive support to victims, trauma, sexual abuse and assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, and medical and mental health care.

The duty location of each CRC will be at a designated ICE detention facility or ICE office. At each duty location, the CRC will be responsible for supporting ERO Field office and facility staff in their daily duties.

Responsibilities

Assist with needs, requests (on ICE Detainee Request Form or otherwise), and complaints from the detained noncitizen population regarding non-officer or immigration case related issues.
Assist ERO officers with addressing noncitizen requests related to parent/child communication and/or child welfare involvement.
Facilitate on-site support of disability accommodations, including coordinating followup, as requested by ERO, with detention facilities upon submission of a Disability Accommodation Notification to ERO Headquarters (HQ).
Assist ERO and detention facility staff as a resource to facilitate the compliance of applicable agency policies and detention standards. Facilitate discussions and communicate directly with detained noncitizens. Areas of facilitation include but are not limited to the following topic areas: allegations of sexual abuse and assault, identification and monitoring of pregnant noncitizens, resources for noncitizens in segregated housing or special management units, and admission and release.
Address ERO and detention facility staff questions or concerns about specific noncitizens, including available services.
Provide noncitizen referrals to appropriate ERO and detention facility staff for care and follow-up to prevent critical incidents and issues (e.g., medical, mental health, chaplain, etc.).
Support noncitizens with specialized needs or requiring heightened attention and conduct noncitizen wellness checks and follow-ups upon request by ERO Field Office and/or ERO HQ.
Meet with newly detained noncitizens during or after intake to answer questions, address concerns, provide brief orientation to the detention facility and CRC services.
Assist ERO Field Offices who run specialized housing units and programs or services that are designed to provide appropriate care to vulnerable populations, such as: a. Dedicate Housing for Transgender Noncitizens b. Behavioral/Mental Health Unit(s) c. Family Residential Centers d. Reunification of relatives and children in federal custody e. Young adult case management services
Provide language interpretation for facility and ERO staff communicating with the detained noncitizen population.
Provide general support, as needed, to help maintain safety and security of the detention facility.
Assist ERO Field Office in removal planning for noncitizens with vulnerabilities and in general population by – researching referrals and identifying to resources in the noncitizen’s home country and developing individualized Departure Plans.
Assist ERO Field Office in release planning for noncitizens with vulnerabilities and in general population by researching referrals and identifying needed resources in the U.S. Planning activities may include communicating with family members, securing resources such as medical/mental healthcare, and identifying housing options or placement in a shelter or hospital/institution.
Develop and maintain a national resource database of resources (in and outside of the United States) for CRC and ERO Officer use to facilitate the release and removal of noncitizens booked out of ICE custody.

Minimum Job Requirements/Technical Requirements

Knowledge of the case management process commensurate with training and education at a minimum at the bachelor’s level.
Ability to work in a multi-cultural and multi-lingual environment.
Ability to utilize telephonic interpreter/translation services to complete assigned duties if not fluent in a language the noncitizen understands.
Ability to adapt to sudden changes in schedules and flexibility in work requirements.
Ability to communicate proficiently in English (verbal and written) in order to develop positive rapport with patients, co-workers and other stakeholders.
Ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to navigate in an electronic work environment including electronic health records, web-based training and communications.
Knowledge of, and moderate proficiency in, common Microsoft Office programs, specifically Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and SharePoint.
Be able to operate a Personal Computer (PC) with common/standard business software programs
Experience in a detention/correctional or residential healthcare setting (preferred, not required).
Strong oral and written communication skills
Ability to create and manage projects
Excellent interpersonal skills
Critical thinking skills
Cultural competency
Integrity and honesty
The Department of Homeland Security’s Personnel Security Unit (PSU) must render an Initial Preliminary Favorable Fitness Determination to be considered a qualified candidate. A Complete Favorable Fitness Determination must be rendered by PSU upon completion of initial, and between, subsequent background investigations to meet the requirements of this position.
Must be a U.S. citizen.

Physical Demands/Duty Hours/On-Call Requirements

Must perform the duties in a stressful and often austere environment without physical limitations.
Must be capable of standing on hard services (cement floors) for long periods of time.
This full-time position requires availability to work Monday – Friday day shift, specific hours determined by the ERO HQ and the Field Office

Travel Requirement

Workday travel and/or overnight travel may be required to perform some of the assigned duties, especially during surge support in designated ICE locations during crisis situations, Travel is reimbursed.

Education & Certification

Bachelor’s degree in Social work, Psychology, or an equivalent degree.

Master’s degree or an equivalent advanced degree preferred but not required.

Maintains current certification in either the American Heart Association Basic Life Support Course (BLS) or the American Red Cross CPR/BLS Course. As per CDC guidelines – candidates must provide proof of a negative TB skin test, as well immunization from the following diseases: Hepatitis B, MMR, Varicella and Influenza

This isn’t just a workplace.

It’s a community.

It’s a mission.

It’s your chance to be part of something bigger.

Choose Vivent Health and turn your work into purpose.

Your Contribution

Deliver Excellence. Oversee with Integrity. Drive Progress. Exceed Expectations.

The Housing Specialist will play a crucial role in facilitating access to stable housing for individuals facing housing challenges. You will collaborate with community partners to expand housing resources for diverse client needs and to increase program effectiveness. Your responsibilities will include guiding clients through the housing process, collaborating with community housing resources, and ensuring that individuals have the support they need for housing stability.

Stay informed about local housing resources and proactively identify new opportunities.
Respond to housing crises promptly, providing support and intervention to prevent homelessness.
Collaborate with community partners and resources to help participants to mitigate issues with credit reports, utility arrears, criminal records, past evictions, unfavorable landlord references, and other issues which may impact housing eligibility.
Collaborate with healthcare providers, especially Vivent Health Care Teams, to integrate housing solutions into overall health plans.
Build and maintain positive relationships with landlords, property owners, and property management companies.
Ensure that lease terms align with the needs and preferences of individuals receiving services.
Facilitate the placement of clients into stable and supportive housing.
Conduct market research to identify housing trends, availability, and opportunities in the local community.
Provide participants with listings of potential housing options in alignment with their needs and geographic preferences.
Stay informed about housing policies and regulations that may impact client placements.
Maintain up-to-date and accurate records of housing placements, lease agreements, landlord interactions, client interactions, housing plans, and outcomes.
Maintain accurate and confidential client records, documenting assistance provided. Need to follow all HIPAA and PHI requirements.

SpringPath Mental Health Services, a part of the Sevita family, provides behavioral health services through Intensive Residential Treatment, Assertive Community Treatment, and Targeted Case Management programs. We embrace a person-centered approach that is trauma informed, culturally responsive, and recovery-oriented. Our dedicated team supports individuals with mental health, psychiatric, or other complex needs to overcome challenges, build skills, and live a full, meaningful life.

Summary

This position works as part of an Assertive Community Team that provides care and treatment for clients that are experiencing significant mental health/psychiatric symptoms, who are demonstrating significant functional impairments, and who may have co-occurring chemical dependency and or personality disorder. The Practitioner is viewed as a primary agent of hope and change and is required to work in full partnership with the client in his/her recovery process. The practitioner has a two focused level of responsibility: first, for the care, welfare, treatment, and safety of the clients as individuals and secondly, for the facilitation of a work and a treatment culture that promotes trans-disciplinary team work, professionalism, cultural competency, and adherence to best practice principles and interventions. The Practitioner has responsibility for client specific and program outcomes. Primary duties include assessment, crisis assessment and management, planning, individual counseling, skills teaching, group work, case management, household management, financial eligibility assistance, and on-call.

Essential Job Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential function listed below.

Conducts over-all rehabilitation goal planning which may include living, learning, working, social and spiritual environments.
Conducts assessments: mental health status review, suicidal, vulnerable adult & immediate needs, functional, living skill, resource, chemical dependency and vocational/employment.
Interprets and summarizes findings with recommended treatment/rehabilitative activities and goals.
Develops and monitors the individual treatment/rehabilitative plan.
Implements the treatment/rehabilitative activities and strategies.
Prevents crisis at the lowest level of escalation.
Manages and over-sees client financial needs, living arrangement services, and monitors medication.
Facilitates transition and recovery support services.
Provides staff and client consultation when on-call.
Facilitates and monitors the civil commitment process.
Adheres to Data Privacy Practices/HIPPA.
Communicates, receives, and writes information clearly and accurately.
Reads and interprets clinical assessments and findings.
Writes crisis/treatment/behavioral plans with differential goals and objectives.
Writes progress notes, summaries, and discharges.
Monitors and records medication administration activities.
Provides objective verbal and written critical incident analysis.
Documents essential activities related to licensure, welfare and safety.
Maintains service standards.
Achieves client specific and program outcomes.
Participates in the 360-degree performance evaluation process.
Increases knowledge and skills based on client and program needs.
Teaches others.
Seeks supervisory over-sight and personal growth.
Performs other related duties and activities as required

Supervisory Responsibilities

None

Minimum Knowledge And Skills Required For The Job

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities required to perform the job.

Education And Experience

Holds a bachelor's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college or university and has at least 4,000 hours of supervised experience in the delivery of services to persons with mental illness; or holds a graduate degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields and has at least 2,000 post BA hours of supervised experience in the delivery of services to persons with mental illness

Certificates, Licenses, And Registrations

This position requires only that license which may be required based on education and standards determined by educational/degree guidelines. All Practitioners are supported in gaining certification as a Certified Psychiatric Rehabilitation Practitioner. The agency encourages staff to seek license at the highest standard permitted by his/her education and experience.

Other Skills And Abilities

The Mental Health Practitioner/Case Manager must be able to problem-solve in a creative and independent fashion. Treatment interventions require that resolution must be sought that promotes the safety, welfare, care, and treatment of the client(s). The Practitioner must be able to intervene in a crisis in a calm, controlled, and effective manner. On-call responsibilities require assessment and problem resolution
The Mental Health Practitioner/Case Manager has authorization to act in accordance with agency policy and procedures and within the scope of the job description. Law requires clinical supervision and clinical over-sight. A Practitioner should seek appropriate levels of supervisory input as the need arises. The Practitioner reports to the Clinical Director. The Clinical Director determines performance competency jointly with the Administrator and with input from peers and clients.
Upon hire this position requires demonstration of the ability to conduct functional assessments, develop treatment plans, provide crisis and behavioral management, provide goal directed individual counseling, facilitate groups, teach skills, provide case management, problem-solve, and communicate effectively, orally, and in writing. This position requires teamwork and the ability to work alone.
This position requires demonstration through training and testing within a designated time frame of the following core competency areas: First Aide/CPR, Data Privacy (HIPPA), Non-Violent Crisis Intervention, Medication Monitoring/Administration, Principles and Techniques of Psychiatric Rehabilitation (including Over-All Rehabilitation Goal Setting, Functional Assessment, Skills Teaching and Programming), Empathy/Motivational Training, Working with Persons Experiencing Mania, Hallucinations, and Delusions, and Relapse Prevention Planning.

As an Assertive Community Treatment service, the inter-disciplinary team offers evidence-based treatment and best practices in several areas. This may result in the Clinical Director's need to balance the skills and expertise of the staff; and thus, when seeking a new hire or in providing training, the Practitioner may be required to have a specialized area of knowledge, skill and or licensure. Family Psycho-education
Integrated Dual Disorder Treatment
Supportive Employment
Dialectical Behavior Therapy
Illness Management and Recovery
Civil Commitment
Psychiatric Rehabilitation

Provides person centered programs while engaging residents in meaningful and purposeful dementia care programs within the Brookdale community enhancing their quality of life. Promotes and engages residents in the 7 domains of well-being programs in a dementia friendly structured environment; including sensory focused small group programming for residents who cannot participate in a larger group setting.
Develops a monthly calendar, in partnership with residents, based on residents’ shared interests. Ensures person centered special events and daily path programs are scheduled and executed as scheduled.
Ensures dementia care programs are in compliance with Brookdale Excellence Standards Tool (BEST), Divisional Dementia Care Site visit tool, state, federal, and other regulations and meet Brookdale’s mission, policies, procedures and dementia care standards as assigned by the Executive Director.
Collaborates with community leadership educating & providing resources to families and associates regarding Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias. Plans and schedules programming events outside the community, which may include driving a community motor vehicle.
Maintains and adheres to department monthly budget and expense control and may manage volunteer program.
Performs personal care, housekeeping and dietary responsibilities, as needed, to ensure service quality is maintained in accordance with Clare Bridge Program standards. Has completed training and qualifications based on state regulations to ensure service quality is maintained in accordance with Clare Bridge Program standards.

This job description represents an overview of the responsibilities for the above referenced position. It is not intended to represent a comprehensive list of responsibilities. An associate should perform all duties as assigned by his/ her supervisor.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in therapeutic recreation, gerontology, education or related field preferred. Minimum two years of direct programming experience with older adults and persons with dementia preferred; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

new_jobs.title: Site Care Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Cortica is looking for a
full time Site Care Coordinator 
to join our growing multi-disciplinary team.   
As Site Care Coordinator, you will play a crucial role in optimizing client and provider scheduling to enhance service delivery and operational efficiency. As a consistent point of contact for families, you’ll collaborate closely with site leadership—including clinical, operational, and shared services (e.g., RCM, Scheduling, Enrollment, etc.)—to maintain a cohesive site culture, uphold the highest standards of care, and guide families through their journey at Cortica. By facilitating communication between families and various teams, the Site Care Coordinator ensures seamless coordination of care. This role is essential in managing cancellations, rescheduling, and implementing optimal scheduling practices that align with client needs and provider capacity. This position requires an on-site presence to effectively manage and oversee scheduling processes and address concerns promptly.  

Cortica is a rapidly growing healthcare company pioneering the most effective treatment methods for children with neurodevelopmental differences. Our mission is to design and deliver life-changing care – one child, one family, one community at a time. Ultimately, we envision a world that cultivates the full potential of every child. At Cortica, every team member is instrumental in helping us achieve our mission!  

Our culture and values guide how we work and treat one another. Cortica celebrates diversity and fosters an inclusive environment, seeking ideas and opinions from everyone on the team. We safeguard equal rights and respect for all individuals, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, creed, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, ancestry, veteran status or other applicable, legally protected characteristics. All Cortica employment decisions are made based on an individual’s qualifications and ability to successfully perform the job responsibilities.  
What will you do?

Patient Care Navigation:  
Guide patients through care pathways efficiently, monitoring their progress and proactively identifying and addressing care delays and barriers.  

Serve as the point of contact for families, streamlining communication and guiding them through their Cortica journey.  

Keep families informed about wait times for services.  

Scheduling Optimization:  
Create scheduling plans that adhere to best practices, ensuring providers are utilized to their full capacity while aligning with the clients' needs.  

Collaborate with clinical teams to integrate strategies into broader care plans, promoting a holistic approach to care.  

Provide scheduling support for contract scheduling processes, particularly for Schools-related contracts, and assist with scheduling activities for Value-Based Care (VBC) clients.  

Must efficiently handle client cancellations and provider call-outs by promptly arranging alternate coverage or rescheduling to ensure consistent service delivery.  

Manage requests for Paid Time Off (PTO) from providers, ensuring that these do not disrupt the overall service delivery. This includes forecasting potential schedule gaps and proactively planning to fill these gaps.  

Manage the waitlist to promptly place clients into available slots as they arise in provider schedules, optimizing both client satisfaction and resource utilization.  

Communication and Collaboration:  
Collaborate closely with on-site leadership team to address and resolve client scheduling concerns efficiently and professionally.  

Collaborate closely with clinical leadership to ensure timely case assignment and management.  

Address client inquiries and requests promptly, maintaining high standards of service.  

Record all interactions comprehensively in Salesforce and communicate through various channels such as phone, email, and SMS to ensure clarity and responsiveness.  

Keep providers well-informed of any changes to their schedules and swiftly address their inquiries or concerns, facilitating a supportive work environment.  

Escalate scheduling challenges in a timely manner.  

Technology Utilization and Best Practices:  
Utilize scheduling tools such as Axon, Smart Scheduling, and Salesforce to enhance scheduling efficiency and streamline operations.  

Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess scheduling success and make data-driven decisions to optimize scheduling practices.  

Follow established scheduling protocols and best practices to ensure efficient and effective scheduling that meets the needs of both clients and providers.  

Assist in the development and maintenance of new Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure scheduling consistency and accuracy as processes, guidelines, and software evolve.  

We’d love to hear from you if:

You bring 4+ years scheduling experience in ABA services or related field.  

You bring 2+ years in client services related role.  

You have strong problem-solving skills.  

Your compensation and benefits

Cortica cares deeply about each team member and their wellbeing! We strive to foster an outstanding employee experience and culture. We also provide a terrific benefits package. Full-time employees enjoy a variety of company subsidized medical and dental insurance options, 401K with company match and rapid vesting, Personal Time Off that increases based on tenure, paid holidays, company-paid life insurance, disability insurance options, tuition reimbursement for continuing education and professional development, employee referral bonus awards, and more.  
The base pay range for this opening is $26.41/hr
 to $33.11/hr
. According to your skill level, relevant experience, education level, and location, you will receive compensation that fits appropriately within the range.

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator, AI Initiative
new_jobs.description:
This position is fully remote and open to candidates located anywhere in the World.

The Pulitzer Center seeks an organized, mission-driven coordinator to support the growing work of our AI Initiative. As Program Coordinator, AI Initiative, you’ll be at the operational center of one of our most dynamic editorial programs—managing communications, coordinating training programs, supporting grantees and fellows, and helping ensure that our AI-focused journalism and education work runs with precision and purpose.

The AI Program Coordinator is a crucial part of the AI Accountability Network with responsibilities for coordinating activities from the AI Spotlight Series, biweekly AI newsletter, grants and fellowships. As the Network is in a period of growth, the Coordinator will work closely with our AI Spotlight Series coordinator, AI editors, and operations team to ensure programs are run effectively and can scale. The Coordinator will work with both internal and external partners across the globe. This is primarily an administrative role requiring good communication, organization and an attention to detail, but we value experimentation and creativity across the team.

Responsibilities

AI Newsletter

Source content for the newsletter by identifying relevant stories and authors from recently published work and soliciting written content
Coordinate the production of the bi-weekly AI newsletter, ensuring a smooth editorial workflow by tasks including but not limited to scheduling writers for the topper, setting targets, and tracking metrics.

AI Spotlight Series Coordination Support

Implement the AI Spotlight Series in collaboration with external contractors to ensure coordination in alignment with Pulitzer process, including overseeing scheduling and event coordination (identifying coaches, sourcing live translators, arranging regional partnerships for promotion, providing technical support, and developing and assessing trainee surveys).
Support the AI Spotlight Series consultants with growing our community building initiatives, including promotion and technical support
Identify in-person opportunities for coaches to deliver the AI Spotlight Series modules and coordinate the event planning.
Manage the application process for training sessions, including reviewing applications and selecting candidates
Liaise between the external contractors, including coaches, videographers and others in producing the AI Spotlight Series online curriculum
Provide support for ongoing development of the AI Spotlight Series curriculum
Coordinate content and design updates to our AI Spotlight Series website 
Build and maintain dashboards across platforms for metrics including website traffic, etc, to improve and ensure data access for analysis and strategic considerations of usability, accessibility, and reach
Liaise with the external web developers and others in support of data analysis as needed
Manage the AI Listserv by moderating, writing content, and admin configuration of the platform to support the growth of the AI Listserv and facilitate community

Editorial Program (AI) Coordination

Process paperwork for approved reporting projects, schedule grantee payments and AI Spotlight Series payments accordingly, book travel insurance, track deliverables, and finalize the project statuses.
Support the AI and administrative team members in obtaining and processing grant paperwork from coaches, fellows, and grantees, tracking status against schedules, troubleshooting issues and escalating to relevant teams as needed for all AI programs, including but not limited to the AI Spotlight Series
Administer the process of issuing programmatic payments to external partners, fellows, grantees and others by scheduling payments in alignment with legal agreements, setting expectations with payees regarding timelines and documentation requirements, and escalating issues across departments as needed
Track impact across our activities and create metrics to help with decision making.
Liaise with the Communications team on behalf of the AI Editorial team, to ensure promotion of events, programs, and new resources are effectively communicated to the right audiences and work collaboratively across the two teams
Support AI team members with funder communications and reports by providing data, reports, and drafting content 
Support the participation of AI team members and grantees in affinity conferences, including organizing panels, logistics and travel 
Support the development of AI products and programming, including the launch of new or special initiatives. 

General Editorial team support

Manage and reply to questions from the editorial email
Support admin team members in Editorial admin tasks such as collecting and analyzing grantee demographic data via quarterly surveys. 
Support website content development by the Communications team and internal website publishing as needed.
Provide copywriting support for email and website as needed.

Participation in Pulitzer Center culture and values

This may include task forces, training sessions, meetings, committees, special projects, organizational events, and any other activities that support the Pulitzer Center. 
Participate in the planning processes for the organization. 

Qualifications

5 years of experience supporting administrative and programmatic activities for distributed teams 
A demonstrated interest in or knowledge of issues connected to tech impact on society, algorithmic accountability, and related issues 
Experience in or demonstrated interest and understanding of AI in journalism and media 
The ability to work independently and take initiative 
Strong organizational and communication skills, handling several projects simultaneously and on time
The ability to develop and maintain agile and efficient workflows and systems that support a complex program 
Cultural awareness and sensitivity to work across nationalities with colleagues and grantees 
Proficiency speaking one or more of the Pulitzer Center languages plus English (Spanish, Portuguese, Bahasa Indonesia, French). 
Background in grant administration or payment processing in a nonprofit context
The ability to center equity and collaboration in all aspects of the work
Familiarity with training coordination, including virtual event logistics and survey analysis
Experience building newsletters with community management (listservs, online communities, or similar)
Experience working with spreadsheets and tabular data
Knowledge of website analytics tools and accessibility best practices

Success Metrics

Your impact will be measured by:
Newsletter Quality & Consistency:
Reliable, on-schedule production of the bi-weekly AI newsletter with strong editorial workflow management
Training Coordination:
Smooth execution of AI Spotlight Series sessions, including logistics, coach scheduling, and participant experience
Grants & Payments Accuracy:
Timely and error-free processing of grant paperwork, payments, and project documentation
Impact Tracking:
Development and maintenance of metrics that support program learning and decision-making
Stakeholder Communication:
Responsiveness and clarity in managing communications with grantees, coaches, trainees, and internal teams
Process Improvement:
Identification and implementation of workflow enhancements that improve program efficiency
Community Growth:
Expansion and engagement of the AI Listserv and related community-building initiatives

Compensation & Benefits

Salary Range : $54,500 - $62,000 annually
, commensurate with experience
Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, retirement plan with employer contribution, generous PTO, and professional development support
Remote work arrangement with flexibility for work-life balance. This position is fully remote and open to candidates located anywhere in the World.

The ideal candidate will be comfortable with regular virtual collaboration, occasional multi-day travel commitments, and flexible scheduling to accommodate partners across time zones.

Salary range listed above is for US-based employees. Our benefit package includes paid time off (holiday, vacation, parental, and sick), health care coverage (including medical/dental/vision), health savings accounts, 403(b) retirement plan, transit benefit, parental leave, and Life & ADD/LTD/STD Insurance.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Pulitzer Center is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We strongly encourage applications from people of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, and veterans. We value diverse perspectives and life experiences.

Questions?

To learn more about our work, visit pulitzercenter.org.
The Pulitzer Center on Crisis Reporting is committed to supporting in-depth international journalism and using storytelling to drive public discourse and civic engagement on critical global issues. Join us in shaping how the world engages with the stories that matter most.

Collaborate with treating physicians/providers and utilize available resources to help create and implement treatment plans tailored to an individual patient.
Work with employers and physicians to modify job duties where practical to facilitate early return to work.
Evaluate and modify case goals based on injured/disabled person’s improvement and treatment effectiveness.

Authorize and obtain in-home and community based services in accordance with the client’s service plan.

be diverted from nursing home or other institutional settings.

Position Overview

The Evening Supervisor & Student Experience Specialist cultivates an intuitive, welcoming, and patron-centered learning environment during peak hours by overseeing library evening/weekend operations, providing mentorship and leadership for student employees staffed during evening/weekend shifts, and participating in projects to evaluate and improve library space and patron engagement, including user research and stacks maintenance.

The Evening Supervisor & Student Experience Specialist also supports Access Services by processing evening and weekend course reserves requests.

Carleton College Library is a member of the Bridge Consortium, a collaboration with the St. Olaf Libraries. As a member, the Evening Supervisor and Student Experience Specialist engages with peers at both libraries on Bridge-related projects.

Working Schedule

This position will work two rotating schedules, which align with Carleton College’s class and break schedule. During Fall, Winter, and Spring Terms the typical work hours for this position will be Saturday-Wednesday from 3pm-12am (2-11pm on Sa). While classes are not in session the schedule for this position will be Mo-Fri 8am-5pm. This person in this position may also be asked to flex their schedule four days at the end of each term to account for exams day library hours (5pm-2am on exams days).

Compensation

The expected hourly rate for this position is $26.50.

Essential Job Functions/Responsibilities

Evening Supervision and Operation
s

Provide circulation services to library patrons including borrowing, renewal, and return of library materials and loanable technology
Serve as the sole professional staff member during evening and weekend shifts and communicate and triage issues that arise during shifts.
Supervise library closing to maintain a safe and secure environment when the building is closed.
Guide patrons in the use of library space and technology equipment (e.g., microfilm, printers, and scanners);
Maintain a welcoming, accessible, and responsive physical environment at the library’s service points and across the library building.
Lead and mentor student employees who staff evening and weekend times to ensure dependable, responsive, and patron-centered services, and contribute to student employee training.
Clarify and uphold library policies to promote fair and equitable use of library resources and spaces.
Assist in processing course reserves by responding to requests made during evenings and weekends.
Set-up and provide support for evening and weekend library events.

Student Experience

Design and conduct user research aimed at better understanding and improving student experience during weekends and evening hours.
Engage with students to gather input in building out our technology, wellness, and other library of things collections so they reflect student needs.
Survey the library space and environment to compile data, resolve queries, and note infrastructure or safety needs.
Assess potential friction points in using library space and accessing resources, and propose improvements to streamline the user experience.
Evaluate wayfinding and signage for gaps to improve accessibility and navigation.

Stacks Maintenance

Conduct regular stack inventory, shelf-reading audits, and missing item searches regularly to maintain shelf accuracy and findability of resources.
Participate in shifting projects to maximize shelf capacity and improve collection navigability.
Coordinate student employees work on stack maintenance tasks and projects.
Monitor collection health by identifying damaged items, high-use areas, and misshelved materials.
Contribute to the moving, shelving and processing of physical library items.

Education/Experience/Skills

Required:

Four-year degree or equivalent experience working in a library setting
Excellent communication and public relations skills with a helpful service-oriented approach.
Flexibility, enthusiasm, and ability to work effectively with faculty, students, and staff, and the general public.
Technological proficiency with demonstrated aptitude for learning new software and systems.
Supervisory experience.
Ability to frequently lift 20 or more pounds.
Ability to use discretion and judgment in a variety of situations.
Ability to handle stress and emergency situations.
Must be dependable and attentive to detail and accuracy.
Flexibility, enthusiasm, and ability to work effectively with faculty, students, staff, and the general public.
Willingness to adapt to a rapidly changing environment and eagerness to learn new skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues at Carleton and at St. Olaf College.

Preferred

Master of Library and Information Science degree from an ALA accredited program (completed or in progress)
Familiarity with principles and practices of academic library access services operations
Familiarity with Ex Libris Alma/Primo integrated library system, ILLiad Interlibrary Loan, Moodle and Leganto

Must have the ability to understand and follow written and oral work instructions, operations, safety procedures, and hazardous labels.

Note:
This position description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

Clinical Supervisor - Bakari Center

Job Code: 2026-SPECIALI-055 Location: Milwaukee Department: Residential Treatment Center FT/PT Status: Full Time Job Responsibilities:

Pay Range: $60K - $70K

What We’re Looking For

At WCS, our people make the difference. We’re looking for individuals who share our commitment to Respect, Justice, Integrity, and the Pursuit of Excellence—people who value others, do what’s right, strive to grow, and bring their best to the work every day. If these values reflect who you are, we’d love to have you join us.

We are looking for a Clinical Supervisor
who is passionate about supporting youth, strengthening families, and developing a strong clinical team. The ideal candidate is an experienced behavioral health professional who can balance clinical leadership with day-to-day program needs.

You Are Someone Who

Has a master’s degree in Social Work or a related field from an accredited college or university.
Holds a current Wisconsin license as a LCSW, LPC, or LMFT, or can obtain licensure within 90 days of hire.
Has at least three years of experience working with youth, particularly youth experiencing mental health and/or substance use needs.
Has at least one year of clinical, supervisory, or administrative experience.
Is confident providing clinical supervision, guidance, coaching, and support to staff.
Understands how to create and maintain a therapeutic environment where youth feel safe, supported, respected, and valued.
Can remain calm, professional, and solution-focused during challenging or crisis situations.
Demonstrates strong cultural competence and the ability to work respectfully with youth, families, staff, and community partners from diverse backgrounds.
Understands the importance of family engagement and believes families are an important part of the treatment process.
Is organized and able to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, staffing needs, documentation, and program responsibilities.
Has strong written and verbal communication skills and can effectively communicate with staff, leadership, families, funders, and community partners.
Is comfortable using technology, including Microsoft Word, Excel, email, internet-based systems, and agency-specific programs.
Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, sound judgment, and appropriate boundaries.
Has a valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle, and insurance that meets agency requirements.
Is committed to positive youth development and helping young people achieve meaningful outcomes.

Job Qualifications

What You’ll Do

As the Clinical Supervisor, you will provide clinical leadership and oversight for the Bakari Center and Multi-Systemic Therapy (MST) programs
. You will work closely with the Program Director, Assistant Program Director, and management team to ensure youth receive high-quality, consistent, and therapeutic services.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Lead the clinical team by providing supervision, direction, coaching, and support to Clinicians, the MST Supervisor, interns/field students, and the Youth Coordinator.
Provide weekly individual supervision and facilitate clinical staffing and consultation meetings.
Oversee clinical assessments, intakes, treatment planning, interventions, and ongoing treatment progress for youth.
Ensure treatment services are delivered with fidelity to the Integrated Treatment Model and Multi-Systemic Therapy.
Help create a therapeutic milieu by modeling positive interactions and supporting staff in their work with youth.
Review and approve care plans, treatment plans, safety protocols, Plan for Extra Help protocols, and suicide protocols to ensure youth needs and safety are addressed.
Monitor clinical documentation, treatment progress, weekly summaries, and dosage information.
Provide clinical coverage when needed, including individual sessions, groups, and behavioral support.
Facilitate or support Making Proud Choices and Healthy Youth Grant groups and collaborate with QA/QI staff to meet grant requirements.
Co-facilitate parent education groups and actively engage families in treatment and programming.
Create clinician schedules and monitor the program calendar to ensure appropriate staffing and treatment coverage.
Support staff performance and development through evaluations, coaching, training, corrective action, and professional development opportunities.
Participate in interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and training clinical and program staff.
Work with leadership to address personnel, staffing, and operational needs.
Monitor youth records and clinical documentation to ensure compliance with DCF 52, CARF, DHS, contractual, and organizational requirements.
Partner with QA/QI and leadership to identify opportunities for improvement and maintain fidelity to clinical programming.
Ensure serious incidents and restraint incidents are properly documented, reviewed, debriefed, and reported within required timeframes.
Ensure staff understand and follow applicable DCF, DHS, confidentiality, patient-rights, and youth-protection requirements.
Collaborate with Milwaukee County Children, Youth and Family Services, MST Services, Milwaukee Child Protective Services, Wraparound Milwaukee, and other community partners.
Attend committee, contractual, consultation, and stakeholder meetings.
Participate in program development and initiatives that improve outcomes for youth and families.
Participate in the on-call rotation and provide clinical consultation and leadership support when needed.
Help build and maintain a positive, supportive, inclusive, and accountable culture for youth, families, and staff.
Protect client confidentiality and consistently follow WCS policies, procedures, and professional standards.

Other Job Information (if applicable):

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means that youth are receiving effective, individualized, and therapeutic care; families are meaningfully engaged; clinicians feel supported and accountable; documentation and regulatory requirements are met; and the program consistently delivers services with quality and fidelity.

You will be an important clinical leader who helps connect youth needs, family engagement, staff development, quality care, and program compliance
—while making a meaningful difference in the lives of young people.
